evidence.quote: At some point, the continued cooling of inflation and labor markets may make it appropriate to reduce the target range for the federal funds rate.
if progress on disinflation stalls, it may be appropriate to hold the target range steady at its current level for longer to ensure continued progress on our dual mandate.
The pace of inflation continues to slow.
For now, I see the risks to our dual mandate as roughly balanced; our policy stance is restrictive
So consumers could surprise us again this year, and that could slow progress on inflation.
I will remain focused on the inflation side of our dual mandate until I am confident that inflation is returning durably to our 2 percent target.

parsed.rationale: The speech is optimistic about continued disinflation, describes the rate as at its peak, and conditionally signals eventual cuts, which gives it a mild dovish lean. That lean is tempered by stated upside inflation risks, strong consumer spending, and a commitment to keep the focus on inflation.
